3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: It was early evening, still light out with just a faint nip in the air. Franc was at a friend's and Deana was at an art class. Monica and I decided to go out for a walk before dinner.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Monica met me by the door, and we put on our coats and hats.

5.speaker: Monica
5.text: “One way or another, I want to contribute to this country. No matter what happens.”

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: Monica beamed at me, her face flush with excitement.

8.speaker: Monica
8.text: “Let’s get back to the house for dinner."

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: What did our ideals really mean if they could be changed so easily? What about the people we idolize?

10.speaker: Narrator
10.text: Ionas had once fought hard and strong against Soll’s judiciary reforms. But after years of the government blocking his every move, he gave up on his ideals and became a part of the administration.

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: As we reached the river, we saw Ionas Crona, the former Minister of Justice, walking in the opposite direction. I remembered that Nia Morgna used to be his Vice Minister. He gave us a quick nod of acknowledgement.
11.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn04_PJ_Route_Park"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_LawEnforcement_Budget_Decrease"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Military_Budget_Decrease"] == true) == false)

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: This was why I had married her -- this passion and resolve. I should have anticipated that, sooner or later, she would join me in the political arena.

14.speaker: Monica
14.text: “We are not weak, Anton. But we are only strong as long as we stand by our ideals. ”

31.speaker: Monica
31.text: “Our former president tried his best. Yes, he failed, but his ideals weren't the reason."

34.speaker: Monica
34.text: “Say what you will, but that relic of the past was and frankly still is one of the most idealistic people in Sordland."

35.speaker: Monica
35.text: “Exactly. He backed down on his ideals and now everyone knows him for what he actually is...”

36.speaker: Narrator
36.text: At that moment, we passed Ionas Crona again. He was on a nearby bench, taking a smoke break after his own walk. Monica plastered on a big smile and greeted him, then turned back to me.

40.speaker: Narrator
40.text: We rose from the bench and started making our way back home.

41.speaker: Narrator
41.text: If that was how people remembered Ionas, how would they remember me? Whatever he had done, whatever ideals he had lost, he must have had his reasons.

42.speaker: Narrator
42.text: Would they remember me as a true patriot? A reformer of the country? What would they write about me in the history books?

44.speaker: Narrator
44.text: I was just starting to understand the meaning of those words.

45.speaker: Narrator
45.text: The sun began to set over the horizon, bathing the clouds in shades of orange and pink.

51.speaker: Monica
51.text: "I don't know. I imagine some might find that stimulating."

52.speaker: Monica
52.text: "Avoiding my question, are we? Very well.”

54.speaker: Monica
54.text: “Oh, it was fine. I caught up on some reading while the children were at school.”

55.speaker: Monica
55.text: "Evelyn also came round for tea. She says hi. She was feeling rather low, though. Apparently she and Petr had a bit of a disagreement."

56.speaker: Monica
56.text: “Apparently Petr had too much whiskey -- as usual -- and didn't behave when Evelyn's father was over for dinner yesterday.”

57.speaker: Monica
57.text: “I hope so. They always seemed so close.”

58.speaker: Player
58.text: “That's Petr -- perpetually pickled. I'll have a talk with him.”

59.speaker: Player
59.text: “It's just a rough patch, love. They'll be fine."

63.speaker: Monica
63.text: “You remember, my friend from university? We were in the Sordish Literature class together?"

64.speaker: Narrator
64.text: Neither the name nor the description rang a bell.

65.speaker: Monica
65.text: “Anyway, she's been working as an executive assistant at the Violet Pictures film studio."

67.speaker: Player
67.text: “I still don't remember her, but go on."

68.speaker: Monica
68.text: "She recently became pregnant, and asked her boss for paid maternity leave. And guess what?"

70.speaker: Player
70.text: “After asking for maternity leave? That's terrible.”

72.speaker: Monica
72.text: “I know, I was beside myself when she told me. And that's not all.”

73.speaker: Monica
73.text: “They immediately replaced her with a younger, less experienced man -- the son of an executive, no less.“

74.speaker: Monica
74.text: “So what? She was sobbing, Anton. I asked her about what happened afterwards.”

76.speaker: Player
76.text: “So she called the First Lady to ask for help?"

77.speaker: Player
77.text: "Nepotism, eh? They must have wanted him in there all along."

79.speaker: Monica
79.text: “She called a friend. She knows this is something I'm passionate about.“

80.speaker: Monica
80.text: "That doesn't justify what they did to her."

81.speaker: Monica
81.text: “As it happens, another friend works for a television station that's hiring secretaries, so I connected the two of them.“

83.speaker: Player
83.text: “That doesn't solve the deeper problem, though."

84.speaker: Monica
84.text: “I know that the mayor of Anrica, Curtan Leste, will be delivering a speech at the annual opening of the Benfi festival.“

85.speaker: Monica
85.text: “I want our voice heard, and this festival is the time to do it. I just need your blessing as my husband and the President of Sordland.“

88.speaker: Player
88.text: “Sure, it's just a speech. What's the worst that can happen?”

89.speaker: Player
89.text: “I don't want you to step into politics.”

90.speaker: Player
90.text: “It's not the right time. Sordland is facing too much political strife -- we'll have to deal with women's rights later.”

91.speaker: Monica
91.text: "This is why I love you. Thank you, Anton -- you have no idea how much this means to me."

92.speaker: Monica
92.text: "I won't let you down, Anton. Thank you.“

93.speaker: Narrator
93.text: Monica was silent for a while. When she finally spoke, there was a chill in her voice.

94.speaker: Monica
94.text: “If that's truly how you feel, so be it."

95.speaker: Narrator
95.text: We walked back home, neither of us looking at the other.

96.speaker: Player
96.text: “Sorry, but I can't make Curtan Leste angry."

97.speaker: Monica
97.text: “What little trouble this causes in the short term is nothing compared to the lasting, positive change it will bring -- not just for women, but for all of Sordland."

98.speaker: Player
98.text: "All right. If it means so much to you.,I'll make the arrangements for you to speak."

100.speaker: Monica
100.text: “My wish is to take his place and deliver the speech instead."

101.speaker: Monica
101.text: “It's not just a speech -- it's an opportunity for real change. An end to centuries of oppression, and the beginning of a more equal society.“

102.speaker: Monica
102.text: “I don't understand. Isn't this something you care about as well?"

103.speaker: Monica
103.text: "Women in this country are still seen as wives and mothers first, human beings second.”

106.speaker: Monica
106.text: “I know I'm not experienced. But I can do this. You have to trust me!“

107.speaker: Player
107.text: “My word is final. You will not do the speech.”

108.speaker: Monica
108.text: “I want to base the speech on women's rights in Sordland. On the oppression and discrimination we face everyday, on the basis of our sex alone."

109.speaker: Narrator
109.text: Monica's eyes were blazing with a fire I hadn't seen since we were students. She wanted this badly.

110.speaker: Narrator
110.text: But I had to be careful with my promises.

112.speaker: Monica
112.text: “You know Petr. What do you think of this?”

114.speaker: Monica
114.text: “Maybe you should. He's your vice president after all. And they're our closest friends.”

115.speaker: Monica
115.text: "A few years younger than me, red hair, scar on her forehead? We had dinner with her and her husband once or twice."

116.speaker: Monica
116.text: “But she's been working there for years without so much as a raise. Something is wrong with this, Anton. And that's not all.”

118.speaker: Player
118.text: “What's she nagging him about this time?"

119.speaker: Monica
119.text: “You know Evelyn hasn't been the same since what happened to her at Holsord Post last year.”

120.speaker: Monica
120.text: “You remember -- how she got fired for supporting Alphonso? Petr tried everything to get her job back, but it didn't work.”

121.speaker: Player
121.text: “Petr's in the doghouse again? How'd it happen?”

122.speaker: Monica
122.text: "But enough about the Vecterns. I also spoke to Janice on the phone."

125.speaker: Player
125.text: “A sad day for journalism and free speech in Sordland.”

126.speaker: Monica
126.text: "How can you say that? It was a sad day for freedom of the press in Sordland."

127.speaker: Monica
127.text: “I don't think anything would have worked. It was a sad day for freedom of the press in Sordland.”

128.speaker: Monica
128.text: “I completely agree. A sad day indeed.”

129.speaker: Player
129.text: “Look at it from a cost standpoint. Obviously, they don't want to lose money.”

131.speaker: Monica
131.text: “They're harassed at work, underpaid, blocked from positions of power... and those are the lucky ones!"

132.speaker: Monica
132.text: “The fact that there are still places in this country where little girls like Deana are denied the right to an education--”

134.speaker: Player
134.text: “I'm sure the parents have their reasons.”

135.speaker: Player
135.text: “Yes, and I will do what I can to change that.“

136.speaker: Monica
136.text: “What kind of reasons, Anton? What could justify this?"

139.speaker: Monica
139.text: “Then more work must be done to grant everyone an affordable education. And in the meantime, these girls and women like Janice need someone to speak on their behalf. A role model. A successful woman."

140.speaker: Monica
140.text: “These backwards ideals are slowing down Sordland's transformation into a modern nation.”

141.speaker: Monica
141.text: “These little girls and people like Janice need to have someone who can speak on their behalf. A role model. A successful woman.“

143.speaker: Monica
143.text: “These little girls and people like Janice need someone to speak on their behalf. A role model. A successful woman.“

144.speaker: Monica
144.text: "It can't just be you. These little girls and people like Janice need someone to speak on their behalf. A role model. A successful woman.“

145.speaker: Player
145.text: “Nonsense. We have our guards -- there's nothing to be afraid of. Let's go to Capitol Park.”

146.speaker: Monica
146.text: “I was going to suggest we walk towards Soll Square, but the guards told me it's been closed for yet another protest.”

147.speaker: Monica
147.text: “I wonder who they are protesting this time.”

148.speaker: Player
148.text: “What does it matter? They are two sides of the same coin.”

149.speaker: Player
149.text: “Common thugs. I will make sure they are punished.”

151.speaker: Player
151.text: “The Young Sords are taking it too far.”

152.speaker: Monica
152.text: “In any case, where shall we go? I'm not sure Capitol Park is a wise idea in this climate, either...
152.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_University_Political_Socialist"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_University_Political_Nationalist"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_University_Political_Socialist"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_University_Political_Nationalist"] == false)

153.speaker: Player
153.text: “You're right -- it's not worth the security risk. Let's stay inside the green perimeter.”

154.speaker: Narrator
154.text: Our favorite place for a stroll was the nearby Capitol Park, the largest green space in all of Holsord. Before the children were born, we had spent many an evening engaged in deep conversation along the riverside promenade.
154.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.GovernmentBudget"] < 0) and ((Variable["BaseGame.GovernmentBudget"] < 0) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.GovernmentBudget"] > 0) and ((Variable["BaseGame.GovernmentBudget"] > 0) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Education_Budget_Decrease"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Education_Budget_Decrease"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Healthcare_Budget_Decrease"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Healthcare_Budget_Decrease"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_LawEnforcement_Budget_Decrease"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_LawEnforcement_Budget_Decrease"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Military_Budget_Decrease"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Military_Budget_Decrease"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn03_StabilityOrder_BanBoth"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn03_StabilityOrder_BanBoth"] == true) == false)

155.speaker: Narrator
155.text: Another favored path wound through the woods behind the presidential housing complex, to a private pond where the children could swim in summer. I was told that Soll himself had it built. The benefits of being president.

156.speaker: Monica
156.text: “All right. Let's go, then, before the children get home.”

157.speaker: Monica
157.text: “I agree. Let's go, then, before the children get home.”

158.speaker: Narrator
158.text: I informed the guards about our route and we left the house.

159.speaker: Narrator
159.text: I informed the guards about our route and we left the house.

160.speaker: Narrator
160.text: The guards followed us with a black Kadilla as we exited the gates. Walking briskly, we reached Capitol Park in minutes.

161.speaker: Narrator
161.text: The guards followed at a discreet distance as we headed towards the walking trail.

162.speaker: Narrator
162.text: As we entered the woods, Monica broke the silence.

163.speaker: Narrator
163.text: As we entered the park, Monica broke the silence.

167.speaker: Monica
167.text: “I was going to suggest we walk towards Soll Square, but the guards told me it's been closed because of the emergency act.”

168.speaker: Monica
168.text: “There are so many police officers in the city now, it's starting to remind me of the twenties.”

169.speaker: Monica
169.text: “I wonder how long this will go on.”

173.speaker: Monica
173.text: “So you say. But I still don't like seeing so many guns on the streets.”

174.speaker: Player
174.text: “I know. It's unnerving to me too.”

175.speaker: Monica
175.text: “Let's hope it has an effect and the threat subsides.”

176.speaker: Narrator
176.text: Leste was one of Sordland's most influential politicians. He had started his career in Benfi before rising to power in Anrica. Benfi's current mayor had personally invited him to make the opening speech.

177.speaker: Narrator
177.text: Replacing him with Monica would likely anger him -- probably not enough to cause a huge incident, but enough that he might use his influence over the conservatives to block me in the Assembly.

181.speaker: Narrator
181.text: When we arrived home, I called my secretary Livia and asked her to inform Mr. Leste that Monica would be making the speech in his stead.

234.speaker: Monica
234.text: "You were a damn communist yourself, once upon a time."

235.speaker: Monica
235.text: "You were one of those thugs yourself, once upon a time."

236.speaker: Monica
236.text: "You didn't think that when you were a Young Sord yourself."

238.speaker: Player
238.text: "I was young and stupid. I didn't know any better."

239.speaker: Monica
239.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_University_Political_Socialist"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_University_Political_Nationalist"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_University_Political_Socialist"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_University_Political_Nationalist"] == false) == false)

240.speaker: Monica
240.text: "The Anton I knew in university never would have said that."

241.speaker: Monica
241.text: "You always did believe yourself to be above the fray."

242.speaker: Player
242.text: "Funny how becoming president changes one's perspective."

248.speaker: Player
248.text: "Aren't you glad you and I don't have these kinds of quarrels?"

249.speaker: Player
249.text: "Being married to a shrew like her would make anyone turn to the bottle."

254.speaker: Narrator
254.text: Monica gave me a quick kiss on the cheek. We continued walking.

255.speaker: Narrator
255.text: Monica didn't say anything. We kept walking.

256.speaker: Narrator
256.text: Monica gave me a sharp look. We kept walking.

257.speaker: Player
257.text: “Can't her husband provide for the both of them while she raises the child?"

258.speaker: Monica
258.text: “But why should she have to lose her job? Something is wrong with this, Anton. And that's not all."

262.speaker: Monica
262.text: "So you're finally starting to see things my way!"

263.speaker: Monica
263.text: "Exactly! I knew you'd be on the same page."

268.speaker: Monica
268.text: "Really, Anton? After everything we've talked about?"

272.speaker: Narrator
272.text: We were right in front of one of the park benches that lined the river. Monica gestured to it, and we sat down.

273.speaker: Narrator
273.text: We had reached the pond at the end of the trail. A park bench overlooked the water. Monica gestured to it, and we sat down.

274.speaker: Player
274.text: “Does it have to be at the festival? Why can't you make your speech another time?"

278.speaker: Monica
278.text: “I don't understand. After all I've done to support you, you can't support me on this?"

279.speaker: Player
279.text: “Women belong in the home, not in politics."

280.speaker: Monica
280.text: “It has to be now. Thousands go to this festival, and millions watch the speeches at home. Sordland's women can't wait any longer!“

281.speaker: Narrator
281.text: Just outside the gate, I glimpsed Ionas Crona, the former Minister of Justice, walking towards Capitol Park. I remembered that Nia Morgna used to be his Vice Minister. He didn't seem to notice us as he walked by.

401.speaker: Monica
401.text: "Serge said he found something in the car after bringing it up from the garage."

402.speaker: Monica
402.text: "A letter. Hand-folded, no envelope. Just the initials E.M. on the corner."

405.speaker: Monica
405.text: "That’s the thing. He swore no one’s been near the car since last night."

406.speaker: Monica
406.text: "But he passed it on after I read it, and the Presidential Guard took it -- standard protocol -- apparently. They check for poison, residue, that sort of thing."

407.speaker: Player
407.text: "Someone got close enough to leave a note in my car?"

408.speaker: Player
408.text: "You read it first? What did it say?"

409.speaker: Player
409.text: "Probably just someone trying to mess with us."

410.speaker: Player
410.text: "Should’ve let them take it before you opened it."

411.speaker: Monica
411.text: "I only remember parts... but they’re hard to forget."

413.speaker: Monica
413.text: "I know. I hesitated. But it was already open."

414.speaker: Monica
414.text: "I didn’t get far before passing it on, but enough."

415.speaker: Monica
415.text: "The Palace was built on lies... from the beginning. Not by the divine, nor the people, but by intent."

416.speaker: Monica
416.text: "I have borne the same burden. I only understood when it came for E.A."

417.speaker: Monica
417.text: "And then something cryptic: ‘Burn the old. Through fire, the new can be born. Until then, an interregnum will bring pain... and the prairie will strangle itself.’"

418.speaker: Player
418.text: "Let the Guard finish their sweep. I will check on it sometime."

419.speaker: Player
419.text: "E.M. knew too much. If they got that close, they could be watching everything."

420.speaker: Player
420.text: "Maybe they’re warning me. Or warning me off."

421.speaker: Monica
421.text: "Already asked. They’ll send it if it clears."

422.speaker: Monica
422.text: "That’s what I thought. It didn’t sound like a threat. It sounded like regret."

423.speaker: Monica
423.text: "I’ve been thinking the same. That letter wasn’t intercepted... it was delivered."

424.speaker: Player
424.text: "Maybe it’s just some bored revolutionary kid, trying to sound important."

425.speaker: Monica
425.text: "Maybe. But if it was a joke, it was a sharp one."

426.speaker: Monica
426.text: "Anyway, we should enjoy the run. It's one of the few things we have just for *us*"

427.speaker: Narrator
427.text: We jogged on for a few quiet minutes.

428.speaker: Narrator
428.text: A sleek cat leapt across the path ahead of us. Silver fur, one blue eye, one green, an Agn cat, no doubt. After a brief look it then disappeared into a hedge with a flick of its marbled tail.

429.speaker: Monica
429.text: "I had two like that when I was young. My mother raised them. They used to nap in the windows all day and vanish at night like little ghosts."

430.speaker: Player
430.text: "I always thought you looked most at peace when you talked about that house."

431.speaker: Player
431.text: "I remember you told me one used to sit on your piano stool while you practiced... like it was judging your technique."

432.speaker: Player
432.text: "I don’t think I ever had a place like that. Maybe that’s why I never learned how to miss it."

433.speaker: Monica
433.text: "Then we’ll make one. No matter what happens around us, we still can. And if not for us, for the kids."

434.speaker: Monica
434.text: "It did. Even when things were tense... there was still breath in it. Like it was holding space for us."

435.speaker: Monica
435.text: "He was merciless. Always left the room when I hit the wrong notes."

436.speaker: Monica
436.text: "Together. That’s all that matters in the end."

437.speaker: Player
437.text: "The past is the past. We have a great future to look forward to. One that we can build."
